Having played the game >650h over 2 years I'll finally give a review. IT IS A BLAST! If you're somewhat interrested in playing horde shooters in a group of 4 I strongly recommend giving Helldivers 2 a try. 

I mostly play with RL friends, but there's a welcoming, active and supportive community. I met a few ramdoms which I'm still playing ocasionally. 

I don't like live-service games as a business model. But I understand why it's broadly adoped. Arrohead imo strikes a good balance between financing keeping the game alive and alowing players to grind for paid content. It's still very doable to grind super credits (the paid currency) to buy new war bonds and paid extras from the super store.  

The portion of the content updates that aren't behind a paywall are usually enough to keep my friends and me entertained. Of course we're all grinding for the new warbond to get new toys. If you're playing just a few hours a week the arrival of new content should keep you busy. If you're starting fresh, there's a lot to catch up with.

Difficulty is sth you need to set for yourself. Missions are categorized in 10 difficulty levels. If you manage a 7 you get all necessary ressources to progress. There are a lot of factors influencing how hard a mission will be: enemy resistance, speciall subfactions of enemies and planetary modifiers. Learn what you can manage. The game imo is meant to be challenging on higher difficulties. Decide for yourself whether you want to play a chill mission to decompress or whether you want to have the sweaty expirience of max difficulty.

This game's balancing issues are exacerbated by perhaps the worst monetization scheme since SWBF2. Players are made to be increasingly weaker with contradictory justifications, only for the progression & mechanics crucial to tackling changes to be locked entirely behind battle passes so expensive you're mathematically better off accruing a part-time, U.S. Federal Minimum Wage salary than grinding the premium currency for them.

And only the first of 23 battle passes are free™, the rest --ENTIRELY-- locked behind $10-15 paywalls whilst, again, being the game's only notable means of progression. It's simply unacceptable when compared to it's direct competitor, Deep Rock Galactic, which ensures all pass content and a plethora of cosmetics for half this game's asking price (US$20), let alone even F2P games which manage to keep *some* pass content available without paying extra. It's simply unacceptable.

Having returned to see if HD2's improved, I can't help but wander back to DRG. Both for reasons above, its lack of shortsighted, manipulative "balance" changes, no animosity toward the playerbase breeding toxicity within the broader community, and a genuine passion and desire to capture the magic which makes the game worth playing.

I had a lot of fun with this game. But nowadays it's gotten incredibly frustrating and I would absolutely not recommend this game to newcomers for several reasons, the most egregious of which to me is the monetization/unlock system.

  1. The game is incredibly glitchy. You will lose lives and matches to unforeseen BS and it really lowers the quality of the game. It's just stupid trying to play a game only to instantly explode because of some terrain glitch so now you're sitting on your chair watching everyone else have fun while you wait to get permission to play the video game again. This game also has a horrible history with performance, with some players having their PCs hard lock, hard crash, CTD and a few occasions where parts of their computer were bricked, along with similar reports on consoles.
  2. The balance, especially for higher difficulties, is very annoying.
A saddening amount of weapons, equipment and stratagems feel completely useless for all missions and all factions at higher difficulties. While there will undoubtedly be a meta for a game no matter what, it's very annoying how if you want to play the game with a sufficient challenge, a large part of your arsenal is functionally useless, just not fun to use at all. Technically possible to win with most equipment, but it ends up being very tedious and boring as ♥♥♥♥ even if on paper you perform perfectly with 0 deaths and all objectives done. Despite having a large arsenal on paper it feels much smaller in actual gameplay.

  But those are just minor gripes compared to my biggest problem with this game and the main reason I highly recommend new players stay AWAY from this game.
The monetization/unlock system.
A majority of the unlocks in this game, the weapons, armor and stratagems, feel incredibly shallow and surface-level. There are some outstanding pieces of equipment that truly change how you play the game and feel very fun to use, like the Warp Pack or the Double-Edged Sickle. But a majority of the equipment in this game is more like "this one's a generic SMG, this one's an SMG that shoots slightly faster than the other one with slightly less ammo, this one's an AR that does slightly more damage with slightly more recoil".

  Having shallow surface-level equipment could be overlooked if it wasn't for the fact that unlocking new equipment is UNBELIEVABLY TIME-CONSUMING AND MIND-NUMBING. First you will either grind 10 hours for Super Credits (the game's main currency) or pay 10 bucks, to unlock a Warbond (a battlepass). Once you have it unlocked, you need to grind hours upon hours (Around 12 or more hours i'd estimate?) to unlock the main stuff you want out of the Warbond. A majority of Warbonds are filled with complete duds that offer nothing to change gameplay and are REALLY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BORING. Most Warbonds have 1 or 2 interesting weapons that you actually want out of them. 
 The Warbond you get the Warp Pack from is the same way. The Warp Pack is amazing, but the rest of the Warbond is slop garbage that isn't even worth taking up space in your inventory, not only garbage meta-wise but garbage fun-wise. 
 You will grind 20 hours or more (less if you pay 10 bucks) to unlock 1 or 2 interesting pieces of equipment that will get old and boring fast since a majority of equipment in this game is VERY SHALLOW and surface level.

  Play Deep Rock Galactic. Play Team Fortress 2. Play Space marine 1 or 2. Play anything else other than this garbage.
I highly recommend Deep Rock Galactic, the weapons in that game are not only much easier to unlock (while still being free) they are also much deeper than the sad excuses that pass for "new content" in HD2. In the time it will take for me to get bored of the Grenade Launcher for Engineer on Deep Rock Galactic, I would have gotten bored of 6 entire warbonds ($60) in this game.

The game is pretty nice if you accept what you're getting into. Personally, I find it fun and entertaining to play as a military grunt with awesome weapons, slaughtering hordes of undemocratic aliens. The hyper-democratic military style of the Super Earth government is just hilarious. The parallels to *Starship Troopers* are impossible to miss and make the gaming experience even better. 

As far as I know, the Grunt Powerfantasy is one of the reasons why the game is/got so popular. Unfortunately, the developer—afaik—originally had a Souls-like experience or gameplay style in mind, meaning a brutally difficult and extremely challenging game. 

The problem we just have to live with right now is that the development team still seems to be split on whether to cater to the grunt power fantasy or the Souls-like experience. Regular (and stealth) patches sometimes favor one side and sometimes the other. 

You just have to accept that the game will be patched in the wrong direction for you from time to time and hope that the developers decide on a single direction. Until then, you just have to keep having fun, enjoying the game and see where the journey takes you.

Helldivers never stops being fun.

Few games manage to create this perfect mix of chaos, teamwork, panic, and absolute stupidity in the best possible way. One second your squad is moving like an elite military unit, and five seconds later someone accidentally calls an airstrike directly on the extraction zone while everybody screams into Discord.

And somehow… it’s glorious.

Helldivers 2 absolutely nails the atmosphere. The gunplay feels heavy and satisfying, explosions are spectacular, and the constant danger keeps every mission intense. Friendly fire being always on sounds frustrating at first, but it actually creates some of the funniest moments I’ve ever had in multiplayer gaming.

The developers also deserve credit for making the galactic war feel alive. It genuinely feels like the community is fighting together for Super Earth, even if we mostly fight each other by mistake.

Whether you’re getting overrun by bugs, vaporized by robots, or crushed under a badly aimed supply drop, the game constantly creates memorable stories.

For democracy.
For freedom.
For accidentally reinforcing your teammate into a minefield.

이름 : 리나 스트란
소속 : SEAF 산하 블루베리 분대.

기록 시각 : 표준시각 확인 불가. 오토마톤 컨트롤타워 파괴 12분 전.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
기상 상태 : 이온폭풍으로 통신마비.
참호에서 웅크리고 있다. 고개를 들 수 없다. 다들 죽어버렸다. 다리를 다친 찰스를 어떻게든 이송하려 했지만 주위에서 쉴새없이 피어오르는 흙먼지는 적의 총탄이 날아든다고 알려준다. 남아 있는 폭발물을 참호 밖으로 투척하고, 코앞까지 다가오는 적들은 찰스가 모조리 머리통을 날려버리고 있다. 그들은 작동을 멈추면 붉은 안광이 꺼진다. 덕분에 박아넣을 총알을 낭비할 일은 없다. 하지만 저 하늘, 새빨간 저 하늘은 좀처럼, 하늘을 뒤덮은 적 비행체들이 쪼이는 붉은 빛은 꺼지질 않는다. 마지막 폭탄을 던지고 총을 들어, 좀 꺼져라, 정신없이 하늘을 향해 쏟아냈다. 그러자 붉빛들 중 하나가 갑자기 더더욱 눈부시게 빛난다 싶더니.
고막이 터지며 한순간에 고요해졌다. 생존을 향한 갈망, 명예로울 수 있는 권리, 군인으로써 누릴 수 있는 용기, 적을 향해 쏟아내야 할 분노. 그 모든 것을 어딘가로 날려버리는 끔찍한 굉음들로부터 자유로워졌다. 자유는 어디에나, 이 전장에마저 존재한다. 그래. 적이 총성으로, 포성으로 우리의 자유를 빼앗기 위한 프로파간다를 외친다면 듣지 않으면 되는 거였어. 아직도 하늘은 새빨갛고, 먼지는 가라앉을 줄을 몰라. 하지만 더는 무섭지가 않아. 이렇게 누워서 올려다보니까, 어릴 때 갔던 바다 같기도 해. 오빠가 판 구덩이에 누워서 올려다본 노을도 이런 색이였어. 아아, 이번 전투 끝나면 다 같이 바다에 가기로 했는데. 알렉스가 유리한테 정식으로 프로포즈 하려고 반지도 샀고. 특이하게 유리의 머리카락처럼 까만 반지였지. 다 같이 계획하고 있었는데, 아쉽네.
갑자기 땅이 흔들리고 하늘이 환해졌다. 찰스가 참호 밖을 내다보더니 수신호를 보냈다. '작전 성공'.
그런데 폭발에 휘말린 건지, 찰스의 뒤로 사이보그가 날아와 떨어졌다. 아직 사이보그로 개조된 지 얼마 안 됐는지 SEAF병사의 복장조각과 검은 머리카락이 남아있다. 바닥에 주저앉아 있는 찰스를 눈치 못 챈건지 나를 향해 총을 겨눈다. 오토마톤에게 가담했구나, 이 배신자. 애국심이 투철했다면 오토마톤의 세뇌는 통하지 않았을 테니 말이야. 내 총으로 끝장을 내주마.

Dear Helldivers 2 Development Team,

I would like to share some constructive feedback regarding my experience with the game. First of all, I believe it is important to highlight that the graphics quality, visual effects, atmosphere, and gameplay are excellent. The combat feels impactful, fluid, and technically impressive, clearly demonstrating the care and talent of the development team.

However, after many hours of gameplay, I noticed that the experience becomes repetitive faster than expected for a game of this scale and price point. Most missions follow a very similar structure: eliminating insects, robots, or aliens, with little practical variation in objectives or mission dynamics.

One aspect that could significantly improve immersion would be the inclusion of missions that better match the narrative presented to players. For example, when the mission objective involves rescuing civilians or children during an invasion, it would be far more impactful to include more believable and immersive environments — hospitals, shelters, evacuation centers, survivors asking for help, rescue operations under pressure, and escorting real people throughout the map. This would create a stronger emotional connection to the mission and make players feel like they are truly participating in a large-scale war rather than simply repeating combat scenarios against endless enemy waves.

Another feature that could completely transform the experience would be the implementation of larger-scale multiplayer battles. The current cooperative gameplay is enjoyable, but the game has the potential for something much greater: maps where multiple squads operate simultaneously on the same battlefield, allowing players to see other teams fighting in the distance, provide support, reinforce defensive lines, and participate in massive coordinated operations. An experience involving dozens of players divided into several squads on the same map would create a true sense of global warfare, making battles feel more epic, dynamic, and memorable.

I believe many players expected this kind of massive warfare experience and greater strategic variety when investing in a premium-priced game like this. Today, despite its exceptional technical quality, there is still a perception that the amount of content does not fully match the enormous potential the game has.

This feedback is not meant as destructive criticism, but rather as recognition that Helldivers 2 has an extraordinary foundation and the real potential to become one of the greatest cooperative gaming experiences in the industry if it continues evolving in mission variety, narrative depth, and multiplayer scale.

Thank you for the excellent work accomplished so far. The universe you created has enormous potential, and many players would love to see this experience grow into something even more ambitious and immersive.

I think Cyberstan really kind of broke us as a whole. 

Do not spend your money on this game.

Sure, at its core the gameplay is fun, but the developers are so obviously on some type of ego trip that it makes it impossible for this game to be something you want to invest time in. There is this blatant level of negligence that is on par with how Blizzard treats their games and communities. 
Even before cyberstan it was incredibly obvious that some objectives were just made for you to lose, and after cyberstan I just stopped caring about MO’s entirely. Why would it matter? I got rewarded for them if they succeeded regardless of whether or not I really participated, and if the MO failed? Who cares. It seems like it’s mostly up to the devs anyways which takes away all of the fun of a live war system. 
Then of course there’s the issue of the balance, or the lack thereof. There’s a perpetual meta of like a handful of stratagems, weapons, and boosters that never cycle out of being useful, and everything else is just completely useless or too situational to be worth using. There realistically should be a lot of variety in terms of making a build, but as soon as something breaks out of the standard mold the devs have set for us and becomes too situationally useful, it gets nerfed to the ground, most likely never to become relevant again. 
In terms of how the MO’s and new content is balanced, it is very clearly all balanced around making whatever the new war bond is as useful as possible so the players are incentivized to spend more money. 
And on top of all that, this review means nothing, because the devs have stated before that they literally don’t listen to the communities criticism. 
Unfortunately developer behavior like this is all too common these days, which is why there has been, and always will be, so many games with a lifecycle like Helldivers.

The Fall of Helldivers 2 needs to be studied. As a day one player who praised the game for going against the curve with its original ideas, its prioritization of player agency and in general making a fun game I can honestly say that is no longer the case. There are so many issues that this game has amassed over its lifetime its become clear to me and many others that this game needs a serious change to ever become like it once was.

1. Balancing 
   The balancing in this game falls victim to the same rhetoric as many other games. Instead of making difficulty an option for those who want it, the developers force it onto every aspect of this game and expect the player to enjoy it. An example of this is the weapons that the game has to offer. The developers have made every weapon and stratagem in the game is some way "mid". Most primary weapons cannot deal with some of the most basic and spammed enemies that the game wants to throw at the player. While I understand that if there was a singular weapons that could handle all things would make the game trivial, there seems to be no leeway on this matter. The few primaries that do have the leeway and can actually hold their own quickly become the best and seem to be the most picked weapons out of the game. With there being so few that fall into this category, the game quickly becomes stale is this department using the same things over and over against the same enemies that the player have seem and thousand times before. Many say that no weapon is bad its the player's skill that makes those weapons good is a cop-out for good game design. I as the player should not look as the vast options of weapons this game has to offer and feel dread at the thought of using a weapon that I know I'm going have to fight against the entire time I have to use it. The developers have fallen into the same trap as so many others by thinking that difficulty is the same as giving players mid to bad equipment and inflating the enemy's health and armor as good game design. Moreover, the developers have seem to have forgot what this game was marketed as and what it should be. They seem to think that the players want a hard game as if its akin to Darksouls when in reality that is not what got the game popular in the first place. Even after receiving backlash after every update they have put out and a ever decreasing number of concurrent and active players somehow the developers have continued to force feed the players with contrivances that is confused as difficulty. The game does not feel difficult it just feels annoying to play.

2. Glitches and Bugs
   Over the course of this games lifetime there are still so many issues that even on day one release the developers have not fixed. Here are some things that I have experienced. There many times where there are invisible walls and obstacles either caused by terrain errors or enemies that have large hitboxes that do not disappear after death and can cause  the player to become stuck in place with the only option to get out is to die and respawn or these can block bullets the player shoots and can potentially make the player kill themselves when using a weapon that is explosive. This is not difficulty nor is it realistic and makes me roll my eyes every time it happens because this has been an issue since day one. Another one is reloading and using stims and picking things up, there have been so many times since day one where I have to press a button multiple times before the game decides to do the action. This is not just a me problem i have seen people complain about this very issue since the games release and it has yet to be fixed. This issue costs me so many deaths that I'm sick of it. I could be standing still doing nothing fighting nothing and i have to press the reload button several times before the game reads it. It happens so often that the games intended way of stopping the player from reloading and stimming such as flinching and ragdolls that its just another layer of annoyance that i have to go through to play this game. Another example of this incompetence is respawning. Ideally and what it used to be is that when someone throws a respawn beacon for you it will drop you down in a hellpod within a set area around the beacon which then the player being respawned can control where they land as they are coming down. However, the devs saw that this was being used to get onto things such as building and tall rocks to try and gain an advantage against the enemy. So the devs wagged their finger and said no no and proceeded to make the game less fun by sometimes taking control away from the player and not allowing them to land where they want. This inadvertently cause issues like not being able to control your hellpod at all or the hellpod being spawned way farther away from the beacon essentially creating another layer of annoyance. However, the devs didn't stopped there they decided to remove the ability to climb up to high places saying not you're not allowed to have fun which then caused another issue that i find so ridiculous. For some reason with the update to not be able to climb onto some things there are moments where i will be ruining and come across a tiny lip of terrain that the game say i cant climb. Even if this lip doesn't lead to a mountain or some really high place its just an ankle high rock that the game has deemed that you cant climb. This has gotten me killed so much and adds so much annoyance to the game. Another thing that the devs decided is that you cant call in stratagems onto elevated so you can be on a tall rock and call in weapons or place sentries onto them. The game sometimes think that even the smallest elevated position is something you cant call in stratagems so the ball will sometimes bounce away from the player making so that you kill yourself by calling in something explosive or just missing a target completely or making it so that the weapon called in is unreachable or in the middle of enemies. Just another way the devs removed fun in order to add another layer of annoyance. These are issues that should've been fixed a long time ago but have not and for some reason the devs have decided not to do anything about these things and other issues that haven't mentioned in favor of adding more crap to the game.

3. New "Content"
   The devs have decided that the best way to keep this game alive is the add a bunch of warbonds that only one to four things are useful or interesting instead of adding to the already existing content. Im just going to list off some things that players have wanted that devs have denied in favor of a new warbond. More customization of primaries, customization of secondaries and grenades, customization of armor colors and passives, customization of mechs and destroyers and ships, new ship modules that have been the same since day one so that sample actually mean something again, something to spend requisition slips on, more levels beyond level 150, new game modes that are factions specific and that combine factions so that the player are fighting two enemy types at once or factions that have captured other factions experimenting on them thus making a new enemy that is a combination of the two, human enemies that have sided with certain faction since there are illegal broadcasts and science that seem to suggest that people of super earth are siding with the enemy, various buffs to certain weapons that no one uses, more difficulty game modes beyond just 10 that spawn more enemies, and more. But the devs seem to want none of this and continue to take away player agency, inflate difficulty,  keep core issues with glitches and bugs whilst adding more warbonds that cost $10 that can sometimes have useless items that will never be buffed that no one will use.
